title.en: The Last Supper: Take, Eat; This Is My Body
title.zh: 最後的晚餐：拿起來吃，這是我的身體

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 26

summary.en: At a Passover meal Jesus takes bread, blesses, breaks, and gives: 'Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup... Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins' — the founding rite of the Eucharist, celebrated in every Christian tradition under many theologies of presence. He then foretells the scattering of the flock and Peter's coming denial before the cock crows.
summary.zh: 逾越節筵席上，耶穌拿起餅來祝福、擘開、遞給門徒：「你們拿著吃，這是我的身體。又拿起杯來……你們都喝這個，因為這是我立約的血，為多人流出來，使罪得赦。」——聖餐禮由此立定，各基督教傳統以不同的臨在神學代代遵行。隨即預言羊群散與彼得雞鳴前三次不認主。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition of the highest centrality (Eucharist). Quoted as public-domain scripture in comparative framing; denominational doctrines of the supper differ and are not adjudicated here.

passages.text: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed it, and brake it, and gave it to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; this is my body. And he took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; for this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom. And when they had sung an hymn, they went out into the mount of Olives.

Then saith Jesus unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad. Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended. Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.

title.en: Gethsemane: Let This Cup Pass From Me
title.zh: 客西馬尼：這杯若不能離開我

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 26

summary.en: Beyond the brook Kidron, 'sorrowful and very heavy' — 'my soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death' — Jesus prays three times while the chosen three sleep: 'O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.' The prayer that names the whole passion as obedience under dread; he returns to find 'the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.'
summary.zh: 過了汲淪溪，「憂傷幾乎要死」的耶穌三次禱告，所選三人卻沉沉睡去：「我父啊，倘若可行，求你叫這杯離開我；然而不要照我的意思，只要照你的意思。」這禱告把整場受難命名為恐懼之下的順服；末了起身：「時候到了，人子被賣在罪人手裏了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The agony in the garden is central to passion liturgy.

passages.text: Then cometh Jesus with them unto a place called Gethsemane, and saith unto the disciples, Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder. And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy. Then saith he unto them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me. And he went a little farther, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour? Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done. And he came and found them asleep again: for their eyes were heavy. And he left them, and went away again, and prayed the third time, saying the same words. Then cometh he to his disciples, and saith unto them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.

title.en: I Know Not the Man: Peter's Three Denials
title.zh: 我不認得那個人：彼得三次不認主

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 26

summary.en: Following afar off into the high priest's courtyard while his master is tried inside, Peter is picked out by a maid, then a second, then by his Galilean accent — 'thy speech bewrayeth thee' — and denies with curses: 'I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew. And Peter remembered the word of Jesus... And he went out, and wept bitterly.' The tradition's most enduring portrait of failure by a chief witness.
summary.zh: 大祭司院裏審判之際，遠遠跟進的彼得被一使女、又一使女、繼而憑加利利口音指認——「你的口音把你露出來了」——賭咒發誓說「我不認得那個人」。立時雞叫；彼得想起耶穌的話，「就出去痛哭」。首要見證人的失敗，成為傳統中最長久的畫像。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The denial is the tradition's classic failure-and-restoration arc.

passages.text: Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee. But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest. And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth. And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.

And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee. Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew. And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.

title.en: Thirty Pieces of Silver and the Field of Blood

region.en: Temple courts and the potter's field, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，聖殿與窯戶之田

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 27

summary.en: Seeing his master condemned, the betrayer repents and brings back the thirty pieces of silver — 'I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood' — is brushed off by the priests ('see thou to that'), casts the coins into the temple, and goes and hangs himself. The silver, blood-price, buys the potter's field for burying strangers, 'wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.'
summary.zh: 見主被定罪，賣主者懊悔，把三十塊錢拿回來——「我賣了無辜之人的血是有罪了」——祭司冷淡回應「那與我們有甚麼相干？你自己承當吧」；他把銀錢丟在殿裏，出去吊死了。血價銀子買下窯戶之田埋葬外鄉人，「那塊田直到今日還叫做血田」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The suicide is presented as text without endorsement; the 'field of blood' etiology is the sacred-place element.

passages.text: Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that. And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.

And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood. And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter's field, to bury strangers in. Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.

title.en: Before Pilate: Crucify Him, Release Barabbas
title.zh: 彼拉多面前：釘他十字架，釋放巴拉巴

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 23

summary.en: Pilate, having examined the prisoner and found 'no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him', offers the Passover release; the crowd demands the seditious murderer Barabbas instead, crying 'Crucify him, crucify him.' Thrice Pilate protests — 'Why, what evil hath he done?' — 'and the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed. And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.'
summary.zh: 彼拉多查問後宣告「我查不出這人有甚麼罪來」，提出逾越節釋放之例；群眾卻喊「除掉這個人，釋放巴拉巴給我們」——那因作亂殺人下監的囚犯。彼拉多三次抗辯「這人作了甚麼惡事呢？」——「他們的聲音就得了勝，彼拉多才照他們所求的定案」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The trial scene carries a long history of Christian anti-Jewish misreading; the record presents the narrative while noting that modern scholarship and churches repudiate collective blame.

passages.text: And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people, said unto them, Ye have brought this man unto me, as one that perverteth the people: and, behold, I, having examined him before you, have found no fault in this man touching those things whereof ye accuse him: no, nor yet Herod: for I sent you to him; and, lo, nothing worthy of death is done unto him. I will therefore chastise him, and release him.

And they cried out all at once, saying, Away with this man, and release unto us Barabbas: (who for a certain sedition made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.) Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spake again to them. But they cried, saying, Crucify him, crucify him. And he said unto them the third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found no cause of death in him: I will therefore chastise him, and let him go. And they were instant with loud voices, requiring that he might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed. And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required.

title.en: The Good Thief: Today Shalt Thou Be With Me
title.zh: 好強盜：今日你要同我在樂園裏了

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 23

summary.en: Crucified at 'the place, which is called Calvary' between two criminals, Jesus prays for his executioners — 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do' — while rulers, soldiers, and one thief mock him. The other thief rebukes his fellow — 'this man hath done nothing amiss' — and asks only, 'Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom', receiving the day's great promise: 'Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.'
summary.zh: 在「名叫各各他」的地方，耶穌被釘在兩個罪犯之間，卻為行刑者禱告：「父啊，赦免他們，因為他們所作的，他們不曉得。」官長兵丁與一個強盜譏誚他；另一強盜責備同伴——「這個人沒有作過一件不好的事」——只求「耶穌啊，你得國降臨的時候，求你記念我」，便得那日的大應許：「我實在告訴你，今日你要同我在樂園裏了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The penitent thief is venerated as St Dismas; the last-moment conversion is a beloved motif.

passages.text: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left. Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots. And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.

And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us. But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation? And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss. And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom. And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.

title.en: The Empty Tomb and the Risen Lord

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 40: Matthew, chapter 28

summary.en: At dawn on the first day of the week, a great earthquake rolls back the stone; an angel whose countenance is like lightning sits upon it and tells the women, 'He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay... go quickly, and tell his disciples.' Running with fear and great joy, they meet Jesus himself — 'All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him' — the founding scene of the Christian resurrection claim and of the first day of the week as the Lord's day.
summary.zh: 七日的頭一日天快亮時，地大震動，石頭滾開；面貌如閃電的天使坐在石上，對婦女說：「他不在這裏，照他所說的，已經復活了。你們來看安放主的地方……快去告訴他的門徒。」婦女又害怕又大大歡喜地跑去報信，途中遇見耶穌——「願你們平安。她們就上前抱住他的腳拜他。」——基督教復活信仰與七日頭一日（主日）由此奠基。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The resurrection claim is the central confession of Christianity; recorded as narrative for comparative study of death-reversal myths.

passages.text: In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre. And, behold, there was a great earthquake: for the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it. His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow: and for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men.

And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay. And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you. And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word.

And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him. Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

title.en: The Road to Emmaus: Known in the Breaking of Bread
title.zh: 以馬忤斯路上：擘餅時被認出

region.zh: 以馬忤斯，距耶路撒冷二十五里

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 42: Luke, chapter 24

summary.en: Two disciples walk out of Jerusalem in grief — 'we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel' — and a stranger joins them, expounding the scriptures about the Christ, until they urge, 'Abide with us.' At table he takes bread, blesses, breaks, and gives; 'their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.' 'Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way?' — and they run back to tell the eleven.
summary.zh: 兩個門徒懷著失望出城——「我們素來所盼望要贖以色列的就是他」——一位生客同行，將經上指著基督的話講解明白，直到他們強留「請你同我們住下吧」。坐席時他拿起餅來祝謝擘開遞給，「他們的眼睛明亮了，這才認出他來；忽然耶穌不見了」。「在路上他和我們說話，我們的心豈不是火熱的麼？」——二人即刻跑回耶路撒冷報信。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The meal recognition scene is the Eucharist's favorite resurrection appearance.

passages.text: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know him. And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him. But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel.

And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and he made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them. And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him; and he vanished out of their sight.

And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures? And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them, saying, The Lord is risen indeed, and hath appeared to Simon. And they told what things were done in the way, and how he was known of them in breaking of bread.

title.en: Doubting Thomas: My Lord and My God
title.zh: 多馬的懷疑：我的主，我的神

region.en: Upper room behind shut doors, Jerusalem
region.zh: 耶路撒冷，門都關了的樓房

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 20

summary.en: Absant when the risen Jesus appears, Thomas will not believe the others' report: 'Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.' Eight days later Jesus comes through shut doors and offers exactly that evidence — 'be not faithless, but believing' — and Thomas's answer is the gospel's highest confession: 'My LORD and my God.' The blessing that follows reaches across the centuries: 'blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.'
summary.zh: 主復活顯現時多馬不在，便說：「我非看見他手上的釘痕，用指頭探入那釘痕，又用手探入他的肋旁，我總不信。」八日後，耶穌從關著的門進來，偏偏邀請他那樣驗證——「不要疑惑，總要信」——多馬的回答是福音書最高的認信：「我的主！我的神！」隨後的祝福直達千百年後：「那沒有看見就信的有福了。」

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. 'Doubting Thomas' has become proverbial; the confessional apex of John's gospel.

passages.text: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the LORD. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.

And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you. Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into his side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto him, My LORD and my God. Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

title.en: Mary Mistakes the Risen Christ for the Gardener

region.zh: 耶路撒冷，墳墓旁的園子

source.work: The Bible, King James Version, Book 43: John, chapter 20

summary.en: Weeping outside the empty tomb, Mary Magdalene stoops to see two angels in white — 'Woman, why weepest thou?' — then turns and sees a figure she takes for the gardener, even offering to carry the body away herself. One word breaks through: 'Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.' Sent to tell the brethren 'I ascend unto my Father, and your Father', she becomes the first apostle of the resurrection — 'the apostle to the apostles.'
summary.zh: 馬利亞站在空墳外哭，低頭見兩位白衣天使問「婦人，你為甚麼哭？」；轉身見一人，誤認為是園丁，甚至願親自把遺體搬走。一聲呼名穿透一切：「耶穌說：馬利亞。她轉過身來，用希伯來話對他說：拉波尼（就是夫子的意思）。」受差去向弟兄報信「我要升上去見我的父，也是你們的父」——她成為復活信息的第一位使者，「使徒的使徒」。

sensitivity.note: Living tradition. The first-witness scene underlies the honorific 'apostle to the apostles'.

passages.text: But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre, and seeth two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain. And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my LORD, and I know not where they have laid him.

And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus. Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master. Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God. Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the LORD, and that he had spoken these things unto her.
